title: Same Cluster, 33 Points More Utilization: Optimizing GPU Allocation Order for Enterprise AI
summary: The article presents a case study by Dharma-AI on improving GPU cluster utilization through a constraint-aware allocator. By reordering job scheduling (prioritizing based on workload type and demand curves) instead of using a FIFO approach, the team achieved up to 33 percentage points higher GPU utilization and 105% more priority-weighted output on identical hardware. The solution focuses on treating real-time inference as an elastic demand curve and batch jobs as priority-based allocations, avoiding static reservations that waste capacity.
key_points: GPU utilization, not intelligence, is the next major constraint in enterprise AI.
A constraint-aware allocator improved GPU utilization by up to 33 percentage points and priority-weighted output by up to 105% compared to FIFO scheduling.

The core problem is managing two incompatible workload shapes: batch-like jobs (training, batch inference, quantization) needing contiguous GPU blocks, and elastic real-time inference driven by demand curves.
FIFO scheduling wastes capacity due to static reservations for peak real-time demand and suboptimal job ordering under contention.
The allocator treats real-time demand as a curve, allocating GPUs dynamically, while batch jobs are placed by priority across the entire scheduling horizon.

Five constraints define legal allocations: single job per GPU per timestep, demand range adherence, contiguous blocks for batch jobs, GPU swap limits for real-time jobs, and no preemption of running jobs.
The objective function balances priority-weighted batch job rewards and penalties for unmet real-time demand, enforcing service-level policies within the optimization.
The allocator runs in 1-15 milliseconds, making it feasible for per-request decisions, and includes a 'full mode' for periodic optimization reviews.
Accurate demand forecasting is critical, with specialized estimators for training, quantization, and real-time inference workloads.
The system optimizes a 24-hour horizon but commits only the current timestep, re-running every 30-60 minutes to absorb forecast errors and avoid the 'end-of-world effect'.
The approach generalizes beyond AI: encoding operational constraints into decision-making can significantly improve resource utilization.
